[LGRA.22.2] **Classification is by production, not by token.** The grammar must
assign the type-versus-binding role by which nonterminal reduces a `NAME`:

```
type_ref: NAME          // a NAME reduced in a type-reference slot → schema / type
binding:  NAME          // a NAME reduced in a binding slot        → binding
```

In a pattern, the schema is the `NAME` that heads the pattern body (after any
`no` / `latest` / `then` keyword) and reduces to `type_ref`; the binding is the
trailing `NAME` and reduces to `binding` ([LGRA.8]). In expression position, a
`NAME` reduces to a single `BindingRef` node whose meaning the compiler resolves
by name lookup ([LGRA.22.7]); the compiler must not depend on the token class to
make that resolution.
